result.rationale: Verifiable in the diff: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` is case-sensitive, while `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is not, so 'Spam@X.com' bypasses 'spam@x.com' blacklist and 'Guest@x.com' duplicates existing 'guest@x.com' attendee. Email addresses are case-insensitive in practice, so this is a real correctness/security defect.

judged_text: uniqueGuests filters by exact case-sensitive email comparison against existing attendees (guest === attendee.email) and against lowercased blacklist entries, while the client schema only checks format. Adding "Guest@x.com" when "guest@x.com" already attends passes validation, creates a duplicate attendee row, and sends a duplicate invite; conversely blacklist matching is case-normalized on the blacklist side but not the guest side, so "Spam@X.com" bypasses a "spam@x.com" blacklist entry.
